cards.explanation: The answer is that He wishes it were burning already. Jesus says, "I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!" (Luke 12:49). He isn't wishing for more time here. He's wishing it were already burning. I think that tells us how much this matters to Him.

The answer is False. Jesus doesn't say He's calm and settled. He says, "…how distressed I am until it is accomplished!" (Luke 12:50). That word "distressed" is a big one, friends. Calm and settled is nowhere in there.

The answer is division. Jesus asks, "Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth?" and then answers: "No, I tell you, but division." (Luke 12:51). I think that one lands like a bakery with no cookies in it, because it's the opposite of what the crowd was expecting. Then He says households will be divided, five in one home, three against two and two against three (Luke 12:52). I think this is a heavy part, friends, so let it sit a second.

The answer is True. Jesus says they "…will be divided, father against son and son against father…" (Luke 12:53). He goes on to say mother against daughter and daughter against mother, too. He lists it out both ways, friends. It's a tough list to hear.

The answer is a shower. Jesus says, "As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens." (Luke 12:54). They see the cloud and they call it, friends. Then the rain shows up.

The answer is hot. Jesus says, "And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is." (Luke 12:55). Those crowds read the weather well, bakers. Two for two, and the weather agrees with them both times.

The answer is the present time. Jesus says, "You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?" (Luke 12:56). They can read a cloud, but He asks why they can't read the present time. That's the point of His question, bakers.

The answer is False. Jesus asks, "And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?" (Luke 12:57). He's pointing them to judge for themselves, not to let someone else decide. It's like me asking why you'd ask a neighbor if the dough looks right when the bowl is sitting in front of you, friends.

The word is reconcile. Jesus says, "Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate." (Luke 12:58). Notice He says "every effort," friends. That's not a quick shrug and a "my bad," that's me hustling like my cookies are in the oven and the timer's already screaming. Do it on the road, while there's still road.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny." (Luke 12:59). So no early exit, friends. That's the reason He says to reconcile while you're still on the way.
